history.claim: In 1968 (2511 BE), iron from a tin dredger was used to construct the Khok Khanoon iron bridge, measuring over 200 metres long, across the Takua Pa River.
history.quote: In 1968, iron from a tin dredger was used to construct the Khok Khanoon iron bridge.

history.claim: The initiator was Mr. Juti Boon Soong, owner of Juti Boon Soong Dredging Company Limited, which was founded in 1960.
history.quote: Mr. Juti Boon Soong, business owner and president of the dredging company.

history.claim: The bridge was built to solve commuting problems for workers and locals travelling between the old town market and the dredging company. They originally used rowboats to cross the Takua Pa Canal. The bridge was used for walking, cycling, and transporting goods.
history.quote: Therefore, a wooden bridge was built so workers could walk and cycle across.

history.claim: Government sources classify the Khok Khanoon iron bridge as an art and cultural site worthy of conservation. They note that the old, disused tin dredging plant can still be seen when walking across the bridge.
history.quote: The old dredging plant can still be seen in its original condition even though it is no longer in use.

history.claim: It is not verified by reviewed sources if the bridge has been registered as a historical site by the Fine Arts Department.
history.quote: No registration information in the reviewed data page.

timeline.title: Juti Boon Soong took over the mining business
timeline.detail: Local databases indicate that Mr. Juti Boon Soong bought the Takua Pa Valley dredging company and discovered commuting difficulties for workers and locals between the old market and the company area.

timeline.title: Construction of Khok Khanoon iron bridge
timeline.detail: Iron from a decommissioned tin dredger was used to build a bridge over 200 metres long across the Takua Pa River, connecting the town with the mining area and factory.

timeline.title: Featured as a location in the film Wonderful Town
timeline.detail: Articles tracking filming locations state that the bridge was a setting in the Thai film Wonderful Town. This is not verified by official production documents, only by audience articles.

timeline.title: Municipality included the bridge entrance area in budget documents
timeline.detail: Discovered municipal budget documents contain an item for the maintenance and improvement of land and structures around the entrance of the Boon Soong iron bridge. This is not evidence of a restoration of the bridge itself.

timeline.title: NBT reported the bridge as a mining heritage site
timeline.detail: NBT reported that the bridge is a historical landmark and was temporarily closed that week to accommodate the filming of a foreign movie.

timeline.title: The wooden bridge came first
timeline.detail: A wooden bridge was built for workers to walk and cycle across the canal, as well as for locals to transport goods, but the reviewed sources do not specify the exact year.

news.title: Inviting check-ins at Boon Soong iron bridge, mining heritage of Takua Pa town
news.summary: NBT presented the bridge as a mining heritage site and historical landmark, noting its temporary closure for a foreign film production.

visit.best_time: Morning or evening to avoid hot weather (suggestion from reviews, not official times)
visit.parking: Reviews state that roadside parking is available with limited space, but this is not verified by official sources
visit.opening_hours: Open all day (information from secondary tourist sources)

iron-bridge.address_line: Rat Bamrung Road, Ban Khok Khanoon

history.claim: This site dates back archaeologically to the period of 1840 to 1881 (2383 to 2424 BE).
It is suggested, not settled, that it was built during the time of Phraya Senanuchit (Nuch na Nakhon), the governor of Takua Pa, to be a wall surrounding his residence and defending against enemies.
history.quote: Built surrounding the residence. It acts like a camp wall defending against enemies.

history.claim: It is related to the conflict among Chinese groups in Takua Pa town, which is linked to tin mining interests. It was also used as a shelter for the townspeople.
King Chulalongkorn visited Takua Pa and viewed the governor's residence on 28 May 1890.
history.quote: Viewed this Takua Pa governor's residence as well.

history.claim: The wall has a rectangular layout, built with layers of mortar mixed with gravel and sand. The base is wider than the wall itself, and the intact section is about 5 metres high.
The interior is divided into 3 sections: the front palace, the hall, and the rear palace, connected by doors.
history.quote: The inside of the wall is divided into 3 sections.

history.claim: The Fine Arts Department excavated the site in 1999, finding Qing dynasty Chinese ceramics, European ceramics, and other evidence.
history.quote: Archaeological excavation by the Fine Arts Department in 1999.

history.claim: It was registered as a historical site and its historical area was designated by an announcement in the Royal Gazette, Volume 113, Special Section 50 Ng, dated 18 December 1996.
history.quote: Registered by the Fine Arts Department.

timeline.title: Began during the time of Phraya Senanuchit (Nuch)
timeline.detail: It is suggested, not settled, that the construction of the wall surrounding the residence and official area began to defend against enemies and chaos from tin mining conflicts.

timeline.title: The residence was still in use during the next governor's time
timeline.detail: Phraya Senanuchit (Iam na Nakhon) became the governor, and the use of the residence area continued until 1892, according to documents summarised by the archaeological database.

timeline.title: King Rama V viewed the governor's residence
timeline.detail: King Chulalongkorn visited Takua Pa and viewed this governor's residence.

timeline.title: Lost its role when the town centre moved
timeline.detail: When the town location moved to Ko Khao Island and Ban Yan Yao, the former residence was no longer in use and was likely abandoned from this period.

timeline.title: Registered as a historical site
timeline.detail: The Fine Arts Department announced its registration and designated the historical area in the Royal Gazette.

timeline.title: Archaeological excavation
timeline.detail: Qing dynasty Chinese ceramics, European ceramics, pottery fragments, glassware, and architectural decorative pieces were found.

timeline.title: The residence as an old town event space
timeline.detail: The 12th 'From Takola to Takua Pa' event was held, featuring performances, ceremonies, and a local food and OTOP goods market.

news.title: Phang Nga Province held the 12th 'From Takola to Takua Pa' event
news.summary: Takua Pa Town Municipality organised activities to promote old town tourism at the Takua Pa governor's residence between 28 February and 3 March 2026.

history.claim: It was the residence of Captain Khun Intharakhiri (Choi na Nakhon).
history.quote: The old residence of Captain Khun Intharakhiri (Choi na Nakhon).

history.claim: The building is an applied Sino-Portuguese architecture built by Chinese craftsmen, and has two storeys.
history.quote: Two-storey building of applied Sino-Portuguese architecture built by Chinese craftsmen.

history.claim: Local sources state that it was built around 1917 (2460 BE).
One source locates it in Takua Pa Subdistrict, while another says Bang Sai Subdistrict. Thus, the subdistrict is not verified.
Community tourism sources categorise Khun In house among the historical sites and old buildings of Takua Pa town.
history.quote: Khun In house on the Cultural Street.

timeline.title: Construction of Khun In house
timeline.detail: Built around 1917 by Chinese craftsmen as the residence of Khun Intharakhiri (Choi na Nakhon).

timeline.title: Khun Intharakhiri served as district chief
timeline.detail: Between 1921 and 1926, the house was connected to the person holding the position of Takua Pa district chief.

timeline.title: Major repair
timeline.detail: The na Nakhon family repaired the building according to its original style and changed the roofing material to corrugated tiles.

timeline.title: ONEP recorded it as an art and cultural site
timeline.detail: The ONEP database listed the Khun In building under the category of museums, architecture, and palaces, and noted the date of data modification.

timeline.title: No readable evidence found regarding Fine Arts Department historical site registration
timeline.detail: The registration year or status with the Fine Arts Department should not be stated until official documents verify it.
